title: Within Thy House, O Lord, Our God
description: Within Thy House, O Lord, Our God in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 17 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Prayer for special Favor”, where the book credits them to the Presbyterian Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: With-in thy house, O Lord, our God, In glo-ry now ap-pear; Make this a place of thine a-bode, And shed thy bless-ings here.

lines: Within thy house, O Lord, our God,
Make this a place of thine abode,
And let thy gospel's joyful sound
Here let the blind their sight obtain;
Here let the voice of sacred joy
Till higher strains our tongues employ

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
